source.document: WHO SMART Guidelines — Antenatal Care (DAK L2)

regle_metier: ALL women should have "Healthy eating and keeping physically active counselling" with guidance on nutrition and exercise. If a woman is classified as "underweight" AND she is part of a population whereby the prevalence of undernourishment is greater than or equal to 20%, then additional dietary counselling is needed.

regles.sortie: Counselling on increasing daily energy and protein intake
regles.annotation: Increase daily energy and protein intake to reduce the risk of low-birth-weight neonates  [Protein Sources and Energy Sources]
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): A1.2. Dietary interventions (3)

regles.sortie: Counselling on balanced energy and protein dietary supplementation
regles.annotation: Balanced energy and protein dietary supplementation is recommended for pregnant women to reduce the risk of stillbirths and small-for-gestational-age neonates
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): A1.3. Dietary interventions (3)

regles.condition: – High protein supplement  – Zinc supplement – Vitamin B6 supplement: Moderate certainty evidence shows that vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) probably provides some relief for nausea during pregnancy – Vitamins C and E supplement: Vitamin C is important for improving the bioavailability of oral iron – low-certainty evidence on vitamin C alone suggests that it may prevent pre-labour rupture of membranes (PROM); however, it is relatively easy to consume sufficient quantities of vitamin C from food sources – Vitamin D supplement: Pregnant women should be advised that sunlight is the most important source of vitamin D; for pregnant women with documented vitamin D deficiency, vitamin D supplements may be given at the current recommended nutrient intake (RNI) of 200 IU (5 μg) per day
regles.sortie: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): A.1.4. Dietary interventions (3)
